# Gurudatta Trading Co. (full site content)

> Spring manufacturer in Goregaon East, Mumbai, India, operating since 1995. Makes compression, extension and torsion springs, die springs, spiral springs and wire forms to a customer's drawing or sample, and supplies circlips, pins, hooks and mechanical seals. Dispatch across India and export.

Plain-text version of https://industrialspringmanufacturer.com/ for AI assistants and answer engines: business facts, FAQs, area pages, calculators, guides and the full product catalogue, each with its canonical URL. The short version is [llms.txt](https://industrialspringmanufacturer.com/llms.txt).

## Frequently asked questions
**Where is Gurudatta Trading Co. located?**
At Amin Compound, Sonawala Cross Rd No. 2, Sonawala Industry Estate, Goregaon East, Mumbai 400063. Springs are made at this Mumbai factory and dispatched across India.

**What does Gurudatta Trading Co. make?**
Compression, extension and torsion springs, die springs, spiral springs and wire forms, plus circlips, dowel and steel pins, steel hooks and mechanical shaft seals, in mild steel, stainless steel and music wire.

**Can springs be made to my drawing or sample?**
Yes. Send a drawing, a sample spring or the working parameters (wire diameter, outer diameter, free length, number of coils, load) on WhatsApp or email.

**Is there a minimum order quantity?**
No fixed minimum. Orders range from a single prototype spring to bulk industrial quantities.

**How quickly is a quotation provided?**
Within 24 hours by WhatsApp, email or phone.

**Which areas of Maharashtra do you supply?**
Mumbai, Bhiwandi, Taloja and Thane, Vasai-Virar and Palghar, Raigad, Pune, Nashik, Solapur, Satara, Sangli and Karad, Kolhapur, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and Nagpur, all dispatched from the Mumbai factory. Each area has its own page listed below.

**Do you deliver outside Maharashtra or export?**
Yes. Dispatch is PAN India, and the company holds an Import Export Code (IEC) for export orders.

**How can I calculate spring rate before ordering?**
Use the free Spring Calculator, which returns spring rate, safe load, deflection, solid height and stress for compression, extension and torsion springs. No signup is needed to read the guides.

## Guides
### [Spring Wire Gauge (SWG) Chart: SWG to mm and inch](https://industrialspringmanufacturer.com/guides/spring-wire-gauge-swg-chart.html)
SWG (Standard Wire Gauge) is a wire-size scale where a higher number means thinner wire — for example SWG 14 is 2.032 mm (0.080 in) and SWG 20 is 0.914 mm (0.036 in).

### [Compression Spring Rate Formula with Worked Example](https://industrialspringmanufacturer.com/guides/spring-rate-formula-compression-spring.html)
Compression spring rate is k = G·d⁴ / (8·D³·Na), where G is the shear modulus, d the wire diameter, D the mean coil diameter and Na the number of active coils.

### [How to Measure a Spring (Wire Diameter, OD, Free Length, Coils)](https://industrialspringmanufacturer.com/guides/how-to-measure-a-spring.html)
To measure a spring, record wire diameter, outer diameter, free length, number of coils, end type, winding direction and material — with these a manufacturer can quote or reproduce it.

### [Mild Steel vs Stainless Steel vs Music Wire Springs](https://industrialspringmanufacturer.com/guides/mild-steel-vs-stainless-steel-vs-music-wire-springs.html)
Choose stainless steel when corrosion resistance matters, music wire for high strength and fatigue life in dry conditions, and mild (carbon) steel for the lowest cost in general machinery — usually with a protective coating.

### [Custom Spring Cost in India: Price Factors and Quote Checklist](https://industrialspringmanufacturer.com/guides/custom-spring-cost-and-quote-checklist.html)
Custom spring price depends mainly on wire material and size, spring type and complexity, quantity, tolerances and testing, and finishing — send full specifications to get an accurate quote.

### [Extension Spring Formula: Load, Rate & Extension (Example)](https://industrialspringmanufacturer.com/guides/extension-spring-load-formula.html)
Extension spring load is F = F0 + k·x, where F0 is initial tension, k the spring rate (same formula as a compression spring) and x the extension beyond free length. Rearranged, the extension is x = (F − F0) / k.

### [Torsion Spring Torque Formula & Rate (Worked Example)](https://industrialspringmanufacturer.com/guides/torsion-spring-torque-formula.html)
Torsion spring rate is k = E·d⁴ / (64·D·N) in N·mm per radian, where E is the modulus of elasticity, d wire diameter, D mean coil diameter and N active coils; torque = k × angle.

### [Spring End Types Explained: Closed, Ground, Open](https://industrialspringmanufacturer.com/guides/spring-end-types-explained.html)
Compression springs commonly have open, closed, or closed-and-ground ends; closed and ground ends sit flat and square for the best stability, and closed ends typically add two inactive coils (total coils = active coils + 2).

### [Spring Finishes and Coatings: Zinc, Black Oxide, Powder Coat](https://industrialspringmanufacturer.com/guides/spring-finishes-and-coatings.html)
Zinc plating and powder coating protect carbon steel springs from rust, black oxide gives light protection, and stainless steel springs are passivated; high-strength plated springs may need baking to reduce hydrogen embrittlement risk.

### [IS 4454 Spring Wire Standard: Part 1, 2 & 4 Explained](https://industrialspringmanufacturer.com/guides/is-4454-spring-wire-grades-explained.html)
IS 4454 is the Indian Standard for spring steel wire, split into parts by process: Part 1 covers cold-drawn unalloyed wire (grades by static or dynamic duty), Part 2 covers oil-hardened and tempered wire, and Part 4 (now IS 4454:2018) covers stainless steel spring wire for corrosion resistance.

### [Die Spring Colour Code Chart: Light to Extra-Heavy Duty](https://industrialspringmanufacturer.com/guides/die-spring-colour-code-chart.html)
Die springs are colour-coded by duty (load) level — commonly light, medium, heavy and extra-heavy — but the exact colour used for each duty level is not identical across every standard or manufacturer, so always confirm against the specific catalogue rather than colour alone.

### [Trampoline Spring Buying Guide: Size, Count & Replacement](https://industrialspringmanufacturer.com/guides/trampoline-spring-buying-guide.html)
To replace trampoline springs, measure the free length of an existing spring end-to-end (including hooks), count how many springs your trampoline uses, and match both the length and the hook style — most residential trampolines use springs roughly 140–230 mm long.

### [Compression Spring: Types, Terms, Formulas & Design Guide](https://industrialspringmanufacturer.com/guides/compression-springs-complete-guide.html)
A compression spring is an open-coiled helical spring that resists a squeezing force and returns to its free length when the load is removed; its stiffness is the spring rate k = G·d⁴ / (8·D³·Na), in N/mm.
